hints: Rotate 90 degrees clockwise can be decomposed into two simpler matrix operations: reversing the matrix vertically, followed by transposing it.
First, reverse the order of the rows in the matrix (the first row swaps with the last row, second row with second-to-last, etc.).
Next, transpose the matrix along its main diagonal: swap matrix[i][j] with matrix[j][i] for all j > i.
Alternatively, you can rotate the matrix layer-by-layer from the outermost ring to the innermost, performing a 4-way cyclical element swap.
title: Rotate Image Problem

content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

content.problemStatement:
You receive an `n x n` 2D `matrix` representing an image, rotate the image by **90** degrees (clockwise).

You have to rotate the image [**in-place**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In-place_algorithm), which means you have to modify the input 2D matrix directly. **DO NOT** allocate another 2D matrix and do the rotation.

solution.approach: Rotate the matrix 90 degrees clockwise in-place by first reversing the rows top-to-bottom, and then transposing the matrix across its main diagonal (swapping elements across the diagonal). Both operations are performed entirely in-place with O(1) auxiliary space.

optimal.description: First reverse the matrix rows vertically in O(n^2), swapping row i with row n - 1 - i. Then transpose the matrix in-place by swapping matrix[i][j] with matrix[j][i] for all 0 <= i < j < n. This achieves the 90-degree clockwise rotation in-place using O(1) auxiliary memory.

better.description: Rotate the matrix ring by ring from the outer border to the center. For each layer at depth layer, perform a 4-way cyclical element swap among the four corresponding edges: top, right, bottom, and left.

bruteForce.description: Allocate a separate n x n matrix and place each element matrix[i][j] into newMatrix[j][n - 1 - i], then copy the elements back to the original matrix. While correct, this violates the in-place constraint.
